reviews.summary: The dinner line in 'In front of other people' was unclear and could read as a dig; three sample lines used UK-only words (organised, rang, colour) a US reader would send; the him/her paragraph stated unsourced generalisations about all men and all women as fact.

The research FAQ said 'matching love languages' where the 2022 study measured being loved the way you prefer (English and Spanish); 'rang' is British; several Spanish fixes: the Jar of Reasons note told the reader to shake the jar, 'preséntale bien' meant 'introduce him', an ungrammatical 'A quien le encantan… quiere', a partner made female against the rest, a 'dejarle' with no antecedent, 'picarse' (to take offence) for teasing, the calque 'se lee como', and a 'la que' with no noun.

Top results are built on quick lines to copy and a Reddit thread asks for short ones: add a short list to text. The 'People also ask' question 'What are all the words of affirmation?' had no direct answer: add it to the FAQ. The 2-2-2 rule and '7 new love languages' questions, seen only for a variant, don't need answering.

organised → planned, rang → called, 'That green is your colour' → 'That green looks so good on you' (and Spanish)

New FAQ 'What are all the words of affirmation?' (and Spanish)
